name: Mount Whitney Trail
region: Inyo National Forest and Sequoia National Park, California
why: The highest summit of the lower 48 states, 4,421 m, on a trail with no climbing: 97 switchbacks to Trail Crest and the stone hut on top.
book: Permit by lottery on recreation.gov (apply February to March for May to October; leftover dates released in April). Day-hike and overnight permits. Wag bags are compulsory. Whitney Portal is 20 km above Lone Pine.
water: Streams and lakes up to Trail Camp (filter); none above it: carry 3 litres from Trail Camp.
dangers: Altitude sickness above 3,500 m: go down if headache and nausea get worse.
Afternoon lightning on the summit ridge in summer.
Snow and ice on the switchbacks until July: axe and crampons.
turnaround: Be on the summit by 13:00, or turn back at Trail Crest.

points.name: Whitney Portal
points.note: A pine valley at 2,550 m with a store and campground.

points.name: Outpost Camp
points.note: A meadow with a waterfall, first camp.

points.name: Trail Camp
points.note: The last water, by a tarn below the switchbacks.

points.name: Trail Crest
points.note: A notch at 4,120 m where the trail crosses into Sequoia National Park.

points.name: Mount Whitney
points.note: The flat granite summit with the 1909 Smithsonian stone hut.
